official.deadline_note: Two deadlines apply: the application must be submitted in the OSIRIS Application System by 31 January 2027 23:59 CET, and it must be complete by 14 February 2027 23:59 CET, since incomplete applications are not considered for the scholarship selection. Radboud recommends handing in proof of English proficiency before 14 February 2027, and the final decision is notified before mid-April 2027.

official.tuition_coverage_note: "A Radboud Scholarship will reduce your tuition fee to EUR 2,771.- (amount to be confirmed). For example: a grant holder in 2027/2028 will pay a tuition fee of only EUR 2,771.- instead of EUR 19,000 (depending on your programme)." The scholarship therefore leaves a tuition fee of EUR 2,771 payable by the holder.
benefits: Tuition fee reduced to EUR 2,771 (amount to be confirmed) instead of the illustrative EUR 19,000, depending on your programme
Can be combined with the NL Scholarship
eligibility: You are not eligible for the lower EU/EEA tuition fee for other reasons

You have, or will obtain, a Bachelor's degree achieved outside the Netherlands, have no degrees achieved in the Netherlands, and did not receive any previous education in the Netherlands (exchange programmes excluded, provided they are part of the Bachelor's degree achieved outside the Netherlands)
You meet the English language proficiency requirement for the Master's programme of your choice
You have been fully admitted to the English-taught Master's programme starting 1 September 2027, as stated in the formal letter of admission
You are able to comply with the conditions for obtaining a visa for the Netherlands
You are enrolled at Radboud University as a full-time student for the academic year and Master's programme for which the scholarship will be awarded
requirements: Hold a non-EU/non-EEA passport and not be eligible for the lower EU/EEA tuition fee for other reasons
Meet the English language proficiency requirement for the Master's programme of your choice
Have been fully admitted to the English-taught Master's programme starting 1 September 2027 as stated in the formal letter of admission
Be able to comply with the conditions for obtaining a visa for the Netherlands and be enrolled as a full-time student for the year and programme of the award
documents: Two reference letters, preferably two academic references
Proof of English proficiency, recommended before the 14 February 2027 deadline
selection_criteria: Academic excellence: outstanding study results in your present field, for example through grades, test scores or publications; relevancy of your previous degree to the Master's programme; and the ranking of the university where you obtained your previous degree

Ambition: quality and relevance of your motivation letter for the Master's programme, promise based on previous achievements and performances, and life experience or extracurricular activities such as internships or volunteering
References: quality of the recommendations in the two reference letters, preferably two academic references
All applicants are individually considered by the selection committee of the faculty they applied to; faculties may apply additional criteria and some study programmes hold interviews
coverage: Reduction of the tuition fee to EUR 2,771 (amount to be confirmed), against an illustrative full fee of EUR 19,000 depending on your programme
Costs of living and studying in the Netherlands are explicitly not covered
application_method: Indicate during your application for admission in the OSIRIS Application System that you wish to apply for a Radboud Scholarship
Upload the three additional documents requested by the system: two reference letters and a curriculum vitae
If you already uploaded these documents for the Master's programme application, you can upload the same documents again for the scholarship application
Resubmit promptly after the Student Admissions check returns your application for the handling fee or for incorrect, illegible or missing documents
official.application_route: Apply for the Master's programme in OSIRIS, tick the scholarship option, and upload two reference letters and a CV, making sure the file is complete by 14 February 2027.
official.study_mode: Full-time enrolment at Radboud University for the academic year and Master's programme of the award
official.citizenship_residency: Non-EU/non-EEA passport, with a Bachelor's degree achieved outside the Netherlands, no degrees achieved in the Netherlands and no previous education in the Netherlands (exchanges that are part of the foreign Bachelor's degree excluded)
official.international_eligibility: Yes - open to all non-EU/non-EEA countries
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: All English-taught Master's programmes are eligible except Erasmus Mundus Master's programmes and joint-degree Master's programmes; the scholarship is funded by the Profiling Fund of Radboud University and follows its regulations
official.duration: Nominal duration of the Master's programme, with the grant for a two-year programme conditional on passing all courses in the first year
official.description: The Radboud Scholarship Programme is a very selective scholarship that offers talented, highly motivated non-EEA students with outstanding study results the opportunity to be awarded a scholarship for a complete English-taught Radboud University Master's programme. It reduces the tuition fee to EUR 2,771 and covers visa, residence permit, health and liability insurance costs, but not living costs.
official.program_type: Partial tuition-fee scholarship funded by the Profiling Fund of Radboud University
official.english_requirement: You must meet the English language proficiency requirement for the Master's programme of your choice; Radboud recommends handing in proof of English proficiency before the 14 February 2027 deadline

applicant_utility.summary: The two-deadline structure is the main trap: submitting in OSIRIS by 31 January only starts the process, and Student Admissions may send the application back for the handling fee or for missing documents, which means the real deadline for you is well before 14 February. Your faculty quota is the other thing to understand, because 26 awards are split unevenly across six faculties, so applying to the Faculty of Science, with nine places, is a materially different bet from a faculty with one or two. Since admission and the scholarship are decided as separate processes, full admission does not imply selection, and the award's value depends on the programme's actual tuition fee.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Non-EU/non-EEA applicants with outstanding grades and a degree from outside the Netherlands, who are admitted to an English-taught Radboud Master's starting 1 September 2027 and can fund their own living costs in Nijmegen.
application_readiness_checklist: Identify your faculty's quota for 2027/2028 (Arts 2, Law 2, Nijmegen School of Management 5, Philosophy Theology and Religious Studies 1, Science 9, Social Sciences 7) and weigh it in your programme choice
Confirm your programme is not an Erasmus Mundus or joint-degree Master's, which are excluded
Get the English proficiency result in hand before 14 February rather than leaving it as a later upload
Prepare two academic reference letters in advance, or written permission to reuse the ones already filed with your Master's application
Treat the motivation letter as part of the scholarship case, since its quality and relevance are scored under ambition
Budget for roughly EUR 12,000 a year of living costs in Nijmegen, since the scholarship covers none of them
common_rejection_risks: Missing the 14 February completion deadline after submitting in OSIRIS on 31 January, because incomplete applications are excluded from selection outright
Holding any prior education in the Netherlands, which breaches the eligibility rule unless it is an exchange that formed part of the foreign bachelor's degree
Assuming admission to the Master's programme implies selection for the scholarship, when the two processes are separate
Applying to an Erasmus Mundus or joint-degree Master's programme, which is not eligible
Leaving the handling fee unpaid or a document illegible, which triggers a resubmission cycle inside the two-week window
Passing fewer than all first-year courses in a two-year programme, which forfeits the grant for the second year
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living and study costs in the Netherlands are explicitly not covered, so rent, food, local transport, course materials and the remaining tuition of EUR 2,771 must be funded from your own resources or from the NL Scholarship, with which the Radboud Scholarship can be combined.
document_audit: Documents already uploaded for the Master's application can be re-uploaded for the scholarship, so there is no need to duplicate effort, but the scholarship file must still be complete
Follow Radboud's published reference letter guidelines, since the quality of the two references is an explicit scoring criterion
A curriculum vitae is required alongside the two letters; a CV-only file without both reference letters will not satisfy the upload requirement
Applications are read individually by the faculty selection committee and some programmes hold interviews, so check whether your programme interviews before assuming a paper-only process
The scholarship's requirements follow the Profiling Fund's regulations, so any change in those regulations can affect the terms
alerts: The EUR 2,771 tuition figure is published as an amount to be confirmed and the EUR 19,000 is only illustrative depending on your programme, so do not fix your budget to either number
For a two-year Master's you must pass all courses in the first year to qualify for the grant again in year two
Only 26 scholarships exist for 2027/2028 across six faculties, with the distribution published on the page
Radboud University holds scholarship Q&A sessions, and questions should go to the Student Life and International Mobility team rather than to the application email
The final decision date of before mid-April 2027 is marked as subject to change, so do not treat it as a fixed commitment for visa and housing planning
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Admission and scholarship in one OSIRIS submission, then a Student Admissions completeness check with resubmission if needed, faculty committee review for academic excellence, ambition and references, and a decision from Student Life and International Mobility before mid-April 2027.
